accel_to_decel_enable: Lets Kestral set Klipper's max_accel_to_decel for you, as a share of the acceleration (see the factor below).
accel_to_decel_factor: Klipper's max_accel_to_decel, as a percentage of the acceleration in use.
activate_air_filtration: Runs the air filter (exhaust) fan for this filament. Sent to the printer as M106 P3 S0-255.
activate_air_filtration_during_print: Use the exhaust fan speed set here while printing, instead of what the filament's own G-code sets.
activate_air_filtration_on_completion: Use the exhaust fan speed set here once the print is done, instead of what the filament's own G-code sets.
activate_chamber_temp_control: Heats the chamber to the chamber temperature for this filament. Adds M191 (set and wait) before the machine start G-code and M141 (set without waiting) for printers that heat their chamber.
adaptive_bed_mesh_margin: Extra distance added around the printed area in X and Y when the printer probes only that area (adaptive bed mesh).
adaptive_layer_height: Picks each layer's height from the slope of the model: thinner layers on gentle curves, thicker ones on steep walls. The first layer keeps its set height. Has no effect when the plate has a prime tower.
adaptive_pressure_advance: Changes pressure advance during the print to match the flow and acceleration of each feature, using the measured values below. Faster prints usually need a lower PA than slow ones. Beta.
adaptive_pressure_advance_bridges: Pressure advance used while printing bridges (0 turns it off). A lower value here reduces the thin spot that can appear right after a bridge, because the nozzle loses pressure when it prints in the air.
adaptive_pressure_advance_model: Your measured pressure advance values for adaptive PA. One measurement per line: PA, volumetric flow (mm³/s), acceleration (mm/s²), for example 0.04,3.96,3000. Measure several flows and accelerations with the pressure advance calibration and enter what fits best at each.
adaptive_pressure_advance_overhangs: Also adapts pressure advance on overhangs and wherever the flow changes inside one feature. Experimental: with a poorly measured PA profile it can leave uneven spots on outer walls around overhangs.
additional_cooling_fan_speed: Speed of the auxiliary part cooling fan while printing, after the first layers that have no cooling. The printer must have the auxiliary fan turned on in its settings. Sent as M106 P2 S0-255.
additional_fan_full_speed_layer: The auxiliary fan ramps up evenly from the layer in "For the first" and reaches full speed at this layer. If this number is lower, the fan goes straight to full speed after the first layers.
align_infill_direction_to_model: Turns infill, bridge, ironing and surface line directions with the model when you rotate it on the plate, so the lines keep the same direction relative to the part.
alternate_extra_wall: Adds one more wall on every other layer, which locks the infill between walls and makes the part stronger. Turn off "Ensure vertical shell thickness" when you use it. Not recommended with lightning infill, which leaves little to hold the extra walls.
auxiliary_fan: Turn on if the printer has an auxiliary part cooling fan (controlled with M106 P2 S0-255).
bbl_use_printhost: Send prints to a Bambu Lab printer through a third party print host instead of Bambu's own connection.
bed_exclude_area: Areas of the bed that must stay empty, as a polygon of points written "XxY, XxY, ...". Some Bambu printers, for example, use a front corner to cut filament.
bed_mesh_max: Largest X and Y the bed mesh may probe. Most probes sit to the side of the nozzle and cannot reach the whole bed, so keep the mesh area inside what the probe can reach.
bed_mesh_min: Smallest X and Y the bed mesh may probe. Most probes sit to the side of the nozzle and cannot reach the whole bed, so keep the mesh area inside what the probe can reach.
bed_mesh_probe_distance: Spacing between bed mesh probe points in X and Y (the grid size).
bed_temperature_formula: How the bed temperature is chosen when several filaments print together: from the first filament, or the highest of them.
before_layer_change_gcode: G-code added at every layer change, before the nozzle lifts to the next layer.
best_object_pos: Where auto arrange prefers to place objects, from 0 to 1 across the bed in each direction.
bottom_shell_layers: Number of solid layers at the bottom, counting the bottom surface. If these layers end up thinner than the bottom shell thickness, more are added.
bottom_shell_thickness: Smallest total thickness of the bottom solid layers. When the layer count gives less than this (for example with very thin layers), more layers are added. 0 turns this off, so only the layer count decides.
bottom_solid_infill_flow_ratio: Flow multiplier for the bottom solid layers. It is applied on top of the filament's flow ratio and the object's own flow ratio, if set.
bottom_surface_density: How densely the bottom surface layer is filled. Meant for looks or special uses, not for fixing over extrusion. Lower values can hurt bed adhesion.
bottom_surface_filament_id: Which filament prints the bottom surface. Default uses the filament of the object or part.
bottom_surface_pattern: Line pattern of the bottom surface (bridges use their own).
bridge_acceleration: Acceleration while printing bridges. A percentage is taken from the outer wall acceleration.
bridge_angle: Direction of the lines of visible bridges. 0 lets the slicer pick the best direction for each bridge. Any other angle is used as given (in plate coordinates, or turning with the model when "Align infill direction to model" is on).
bridge_density: Spacing of the lines on visible bridges. 100% puts the lines side by side, but bridge lines sag and shrink, so a little more (up to about 125%) gives a smoother, stronger bridge. Below 100% leaves gaps that cool faster and sag less, at the cost of strength and looks.
bridge_flow: How much material visible bridge lines get. Above 1 adds material at the same spacing for better contact and strength. Below 1 uses less material and thinner lines, which can reduce sagging.
bridge_line_width: Line width of bridges. A percentage is taken from the nozzle diameter, up to 100%. 0 uses the same width as internal solid infill. Thinner lines go well with a higher bridge density or bridge flow.
bridge_no_support: Don't put support under bridges. Short bridges print fine without it, and supporting whole bridges makes support much larger.
bridge_speed: Speed of visible bridges. When "Slow down for curled perimeters" is off or classic overhang mode is on, overhanging walls with less than 13% support also use this speed.
brim_ears: Draw brim only at the sharp corners of the model.
brim_ears_detection_length: The outline is simplified before sharp corners are looked for. This is the smallest detail kept when simplifying. 0 turns simplifying off.
brim_ears_max_angle: Corners sharper than this angle get a brim ear. 0 gives no brim at all, about 180 puts brim on everything except straight runs.
brim_flow_ratio: Flow multiplier for the brim, applied on top of the filament's flow ratio and the object's flow ratio. The first layer flow ratio does not change it.
brim_object_gap: Gap between the brim and the part, so the brim comes off more easily.
brim_type: Where a brim is added: outside the part, inside its holes, both, only where you painted it, as mouse ears, or none. Auto works out the width for each part.
brim_use_efc_outline: Shape the brim around the first layer after elephant foot compensation has shrunk it, instead of around the original outline. Useful when the compensation changes the first layer a lot.
brim_width: Distance from the part to the outermost brim line.
chamber_minimal_temperature: The print starts once the chamber reaches this temperature, while it keeps heating toward the target. For example target 60 and minimal 50 starts printing at 50°C.
chamber_temperature: Chamber temperature for this filament. A warm chamber helps materials like ABS, ASA, PC and PA warp less and bond better between layers, but makes cooling less effective for PLA, PETG and TPU. Used by printers that can heat or control their chamber.
change_extrusion_role_gcode: G-code added whenever the kind of line being printed changes (for example from wall to infill).
change_filament_gcode: G-code added at every filament change, including the T commands that switch tools.
close_additional_fan_first_x_layers: The auxiliary fan stays off for this many layers at the start.
close_fan_the_first_x_layers: All cooling fans stay off for this many layers at the start, which helps the first layers stick to the plate.
combine_brims: Merge brims that come close to each other into one. A bigger brim area sticks better.
compatible_printers_condition: An expression on the printer profile's settings. The profile is offered only for printers where it is true.
compatible_prints_condition: An expression on the process profile's settings. The profile is offered only with processes where it is true.
complete_print_exhaust_fan_speed: Exhaust fan speed after the print has finished.
cool_plate_temp: Bed temperature on the Cool Plate after the first layer. 0 means this filament should not be printed on the Cool Plate.
cool_plate_temp_initial_layer: Bed temperature on the Cool Plate for the first layer. 0 means this filament should not be printed on the Cool Plate.
cooling_tube_length: Length of the cooling tube, which limits how far cooling moves can go inside it.
cooling_tube_retraction: Distance from the nozzle tip to the middle of the cooling tube.
counterbore_hole_bridging: How counterbored holes are printed without support: no bridging, a partial bridge over part of the open area, or a full sacrificial layer that you drill or cut out afterwards.
curr_bed_type: The build plate you are printing on. It decides which bed temperatures are used.
default_acceleration: Acceleration for printing and travel, except on the first layer, when no feature sets its own.
default_bed_type: The plate this printer starts with.
default_filament_colour: Color shown for this filament. Right click resets it to the profile's color.
default_filament_profile: Filament profile picked when you switch to this printer.
default_jerk: Jerk used when no feature sets its own.
default_junction_deviation: Marlin's junction deviation, which replaces the older XY jerk setting.
default_nozzle_volume_type: Nozzle type the printer's extruders start with: standard or high flow.
default_print_profile: Process profile picked when you switch to this printer.
deretraction_speed: Speed of pushing filament back after a retraction. 0 uses the retraction speed.
detect_narrow_internal_solid_infill: Find narrow internal solid areas and fill them with a concentric pattern, which prints faster there. Otherwise rectilinear is used.
detect_overhang_wall: Measure how far each wall overhangs (relative to the line width) and print it at the matching overhang speed. Fully overhanging walls use the bridge speed.
detect_thin_wall: Print walls too thin for two lines as a single line. Such walls are not closed loops and may not print as cleanly.
disable_m73: Leave out the M73 commands that tell the printer how much print time is left.
dont_filter_internal_bridges: Normally small internal bridges are skipped and solid infill goes straight over the sparse infill, which is faster. On sloped or curved tops this can cause pillowing; keeping more internal bridges (limited or no filtering) helps there.
dont_slow_down_outer_wall: Keep outer walls at their normal speed even when a layer is slowed down to meet the minimum layer time. Keeps the surface finish even, which matters for glossy or silk filaments and very fast printers.
draft_shield: Builds the skirt up as a wall around the parts, as tall as the tallest one, to shield ABS or ASA from drafts that cause warping. Mostly useful on open printers. Needs a skirt.
during_print_exhaust_fan_speed: Exhaust fan speed while printing. Overrides the speed set in the filament's G-code.
elefant_foot_compensation: Shrinks the first layer by this much to cancel the bulge (elephant foot) where it is squashed onto the plate.
elefant_foot_compensation_layers: Number of layers the elephant foot compensation spreads over. The first layer is shrunk the full amount, and each layer after that a little less, until this layer.
elefant_foot_layers_density: Density of the internal solid infill in the elephant foot compensation layers. This is the value for the second layer, and the layers above get denser until the last compensated layer.
emit_machine_limits_to_gcode: Write the machine limits (speeds, accelerations, jerk) into the G-code. Ignored for Klipper printers.
enable_arc_fitting: Write curves as G2 and G3 arc moves instead of many short lines, within the slicing resolution. Not recommended for Klipper, which splits arcs back into lines and gains nothing from them.
enable_extra_bridge_layer: Prints a second bridge layer over internal and/or external bridges, so the solid infill above sits on better support. Helps most on fast printers, where bridges sag more. Beta.
enable_filament_dynamic_map: Let the printer change which filament slot is used during the print.
enable_filament_ramming: Ram the filament (push it with a quick pattern) before it is unloaded, which shapes the tip for a clean filament change.
enable_overhang_bridge_fan: Use a separate part cooling fan speed for overhangs and bridges. Extra cooling there improves their shape and reduces curling.
enable_overhang_speed: Print overhangs slower, depending on how much they overhang.
enable_power_loss_recovery: Whether the print can resume after a power cut. "Printer configuration" leaves it to the printer's own setting. Works with Bambu Lab and Marlin 2 printers.
enable_pressure_advance: Use the pressure advance value set here. It replaces the printer's own automatic calibration result.
enable_prime_tower: Prints a prime (wipe) tower beside the parts. Each filament or nozzle change cleans and refills the nozzle on the tower instead of on the parts, which keeps the parts free of blobs and color bleed.
enable_tower_interface_cooldown_during_t: When the nozzle runs hotter for interface layers, drop it back to the print temperature as the prime tower starts, so it cools while printing the tower.
enable_tower_interface_features: Print the prime tower differently where two materials meet, for a better bond and cleaner changes.
enable_wrapping_detection: Let the printer watch for filament clumping around the nozzle.
enforce_support_layers: Always print support for this many layers from the bottom, even when support is off or the angle would not call for it. Helps very small or thin parts stick to the plate.
eng_plate_temp: Bed temperature on the Engineering Plate after the first layer. 0 means this filament should not be printed on the Engineering Plate.
eng_plate_temp_initial_layer: Bed temperature on the Engineering Plate for the first layer. 0 means this filament should not be printed on the Engineering Plate.
ensure_vertical_shell_thickness: Adds solid infill near sloped surfaces so the shell stays as thick as the top and bottom layers. None adds none (careful with sloped models). Critical only skips walls. Moderate adds it only on clearly sloped areas. All adds it everywhere it is needed.
exclude_object: Add EXCLUDE_OBJECT markers to the G-code, so single objects can be cancelled during the print (Klipper).
extra_loading_move: Extra distance when loading filament from the parking position. 0 loads exactly as far as it was unloaded, positive loads further, negative stops short.
extra_perimeters_on_overhangs: Add extra wall lines over steep overhangs and over areas where bridges have nothing to anchor to.
extra_solid_infills: Make chosen layers fully solid. N makes every Nth layer solid, N#K makes K layers solid every N layers (5# is the same as 5#1), and a list like 1,7,9 picks exact layers. Layers count from 1.
extruder: Extruder used for this object, unless a more specific setting picks one. Overrides the wall and infill extruders, but not the support ones.
extruder_ams_count: Number of AMS units on each extruder.
extruder_clearance_height_to_lid: Distance from the nozzle tip to the lid. Used to avoid collisions when printing one object at a time.
extruder_clearance_height_to_rod: Distance from the nozzle tip to the lower rod of the gantry. Used to avoid collisions when printing one object at a time.
extruder_clearance_radius: Radius around the nozzle that must stay clear. Used to avoid collisions when printing one object at a time.
extruder_colour: Color for this extruder in the interface only.
extruder_offset: How far each extruder sits from the first one, for printers whose firmware does not handle it. Positive values, subtracted from the coordinates in the G-code.
extruder_printable_height: Highest this extruder can print, limited by the printer's mechanics.
extruder_type: Direct drive or Bowden. Only used as the starting value for pressure advance calibration (Bowden needs more). It does not change normal slicing.
extruder_variant_list: The extruder variants this printer has.
extrusion_rate_smoothing_external_perime: Smooth the flow changes only on outer walls and overhangs, where sudden speed changes show, and leave hidden features at full speed.
fan_cooling_layer_time: Layers that take less time than this turn on the part cooling fan. The fan speed goes from the minimum toward the maximum as the layer time gets shorter.
fan_kickstart: Run the fan at full speed for this many seconds before dropping to the requested speed, so fans that stall at low power get spinning.
fan_max_speed: Highest part cooling fan speed when cooling speeds up for short layers.
fan_speedup_overhangs: Start the fan early only for overhangs.
fan_speedup_time: Turn the fan on this many seconds before it is needed, so it is already spinning (fractions of a second work). The timing is estimated from the G0 and G1 moves only and ignores acceleration, and does not work with arc moves. The first layers with no cooling are not affected.
filament_adaptive_volumetric_speed: Limit the flow to the lower of two values: the fitted flow for each line width and layer height, and your max volumetric speed. Off uses only your max volumetric speed. Experimental.
filament_adhesiveness_category: Group this filament belongs to, used to check which filaments stick to each other.
filament_change_extrusion_role_gcode: G-code added for this filament whenever the kind of line being printed changes.
filament_change_length: Length of filament pushed out of the old extruder before switching extruders, which reduces oozing.
filament_colour: Color of this filament in the interface only.
filament_cooling_before_tower: How far the nozzle temperature drops before it moves to the prime tower.
filament_cooling_final_speed: Speed the cooling moves build up to.
filament_cooling_initial_speed: Speed of the first cooling move. The following ones get faster.
filament_cooling_moves: Number of back and forth moves in the cooling tube that cool the filament tip before it is unloaded.
filament_cost: Price per kilogram, for the cost estimate only.
filament_density: Density of the filament, for the weight estimate only.
filament_diameter: Diameter of the filament. Every extrusion amount in the G-code is calculated from it, so it must be accurate.
filament_end_gcode: G-code added when this filament finishes printing.
filament_extruder_id: Which extruder this filament belongs to.
filament_extruder_variant: The extruder variant this filament is set up for.
filament_flow_ratio: Scales all extrusion of this filament. Plastics change volume as they melt and cool, so the right amount differs a little per filament. Usually between 0.95 and 1.05. Calibrate it with the flow rate test.
filament_flush_temp: Nozzle temperature while flushing this filament. 0 uses the top of its recommended range.
filament_flush_volumetric_speed: Flow while flushing this filament. 0 uses its max volumetric speed.
filament_ironing_flow: Ironing flow for this filament, instead of the process setting. Too much gives an over extruded surface.
filament_ironing_inset: How far ironing stays from the edges for this filament, instead of the process setting.
filament_ironing_spacing: Ironing line spacing for this filament, instead of the process setting.
filament_ironing_speed: Ironing speed for this filament, instead of the process setting.
filament_is_support: This filament is meant for supports and support interfaces.
filament_loading_speed: Speed of loading the filament at the prime tower.
filament_loading_speed_start: Speed at the very start of loading.
filament_map: Which extruder each filament goes to.
filament_map_mode: How filaments are assigned to extruders on this plate: automatically for the least flushing, automatically to match the loaded filaments, by hand, or the printer's default.
filament_max_volumetric_speed: Most plastic the hot end can melt per second. Every speed is limited so the flow stays below this. Cannot be 0.
filament_minimal_purge_on_wipe_tower: Smallest amount purged on the prime tower after a change, before purging into infill or support. Right after loading, the filament's position and pressure in the nozzle are not settled, so this is always printed on the tower first.
filament_multitool_ramming: On printers with several separate tools, quickly push a little filament out on the prime tower just before each tool change, which shapes the tip for the next load.
filament_multitool_ramming_flow: Flow of the ramming before a tool change.
filament_multitool_ramming_volume: Amount of filament rammed before a tool change.
filament_notes: Your own notes about this filament.
filament_printable: Whether this filament can be printed by the extruder.
filament_ramming_parameters: Ramming settings, edited in the ramming dialog.
filament_shrink: How big the part is after cooling, in percent (94% if 100 mm comes out as 94 mm). The part is scaled up in X and Y to make up for it. With several filaments, use the same value for all of them.
filament_shrinkage_compensation_z: How tall the part is after cooling, in percent (94% if 100 mm comes out as 94 mm). The part is scaled up in Z to make up for it.
filament_soluble: This filament dissolves (for example in water), and is meant for supports and support interfaces.
filament_stamping_distance: When not 0, the filament is pushed this far toward the nozzle between the cooling moves ("stamping") and pulled back again.
filament_start_gcode: G-code added when this filament starts printing.
filament_toolchange_delay: Wait this long after unloading. Flexible filaments sometimes need time to shrink back before the next change works reliably.
filament_tower_interface_pre_extrusion_d: Pre-extrusion distance on the prime tower where two materials meet.
filament_tower_interface_pre_extrusion_l: Pre-extrusion length on the prime tower where two materials meet.
filament_tower_interface_print_temp: Nozzle temperature on the prime tower where two materials meet. -1 uses the top of the recommended range.
filament_tower_interface_purge_volume: Purge length on the prime tower where two materials meet.
filament_tower_ironing_area: Area ironed on the prime tower where two materials meet.
filament_type: Material of the filament (PLA, PETG, ABS and so on).
filament_unloading_speed: Speed of unloading at the prime tower, after the first part right after ramming.
filament_unloading_speed_start: Speed of pulling the tip out right after ramming.
filament_vendor: Maker of the filament, for display only.
file_start_gcode: G-code at the very top of the file, before anything else. For information some firmware reads from the first lines, like print time or filament use. Placeholders such as {print_time_sec} work.
filename_format: How exported files are named. Placeholders such as {input_filename_base} work.
fill_multiline: Print each infill line as several lines side by side, for patterns that support it.
filter_out_gap_fill: Skip gap fill shorter than this. Applies to top, bottom and solid infill, and to wall gaps with the classic wall generator.
first_layer_flow_ratio: Extra flow multiplier for the first layer, on top of each line type's own flow. Brim and skirt are not affected.
first_x_layer_fan_speed: Auxiliary fan speed for the first layers set above only.
flashforge_serial_number: The printer's serial number, needed by Flashforge's local connection.
flush_into_infill: Purge after filament changes into the parts' infill instead of the prime tower, which wastes less and prints faster. Mixed colors can show through clear walls. Needs the prime tower.
flush_into_objects: Use this object to purge after filament changes, which saves filament and time but mixes its colors. Needs the prime tower.
flush_into_support: Purge after filament changes into the support, which wastes less and prints faster. Needs the prime tower.
flush_multiplier: Scales every amount in the purging volume table.
flush_volumes_matrix: How much (mm³) to purge on the prime tower when changing from one filament to another, for every pair.
flush_volumes_vector: Purge amounts when loading or unloading each filament, used to fill in the full table more easily.
full_fan_speed_layer: The part cooling fan ramps up evenly from the last layer without cooling and reaches full speed at this layer. If this number is lower, the fan goes straight to full speed after the layers without cooling.
fuzzy_skin: Moves the nozzle randomly while printing walls for a rough, textured surface. Choose which walls get it: outer, holes, both, all walls, only painted areas, or none.
fuzzy_skin_first_layer: Also make the first layer fuzzy.
fuzzy_skin_layers_between_ripple_offset: How many layers in a row keep the same ripple position before the offset shifts it. 1 shifts every other layer, 2 shifts every second pair, and so on.
fuzzy_skin_mode: How the texture is made (Arachne wall generator only). Displacement moves the nozzle sideways from the wall line. Extrusion changes the amount of plastic along the line instead. Combined does both.
fuzzy_skin_noise_type: Kind of noise for the texture: classic random, Perlin (smoother and more even), billow (lumpier), ridged multifractal (sharp ridges), Voronoi (cell pattern) or ripple (regular waves).
fuzzy_skin_octaves: Layers of detail in the noise. More gives finer detail and slower slicing.
fuzzy_skin_persistence: How strong the finer noise layers are. Lower gives smoother texture.
fuzzy_skin_point_distance: Average distance between the random points along each wall line.
fuzzy_skin_ripple_offset: How far the ripple pattern shifts along the wall each time, as a share of one wave. 0% keeps every layer the same, 50% puts peaks over valleys, 100% looks the same as 0%.
fuzzy_skin_ripples_per_layer: Number of full waves around each layer.
fuzzy_skin_scale: Size of the noise features. Bigger values give bigger bumps.
fuzzy_skin_thickness: How far the nozzle may move off the wall line. Keep it below the outer wall line width.
gap_fill_flow_ratio: Flow multiplier for gap fill, applied on top of the filament's flow ratio and the object's flow ratio.
gap_fill_target: Which solid surfaces get gap fill: everywhere (top, bottom and internal solid), only top and bottom, or nowhere. The shortest gap filled is set by "Filter out tiny gaps". Wall gaps are not affected.
gap_infill_speed: Speed of gap fill. Gaps have uneven line widths and print better slower.
gcode_comments: Write a comment explaining every G-code line. The file gets much bigger, which can slow down printing from an SD card.
gcode_flavor: Which firmware dialect the printer understands.
gcode_label_objects: Mark in the G-code which object each move belongs to, so objects can be cancelled during the print (for example with OctoPrint's Cancel Object). Does not work with single extruder multi material or with purging into objects or infill.
gyroid_optimized: At low densities, tightens the gyroid's waves vertically so the walls inside are shorter and resist buckling under top-down loads better. Uses the same filament. Makes no difference around 30% density and above. Experimental.
has_filament_switcher: The printer has a filament changer such as an AMS.
high_current_on_filament_swap: Raise the extruder motor current during filament changes, for fast ramming and for pushing a badly shaped tip through.
hole_to_polyhole: Turn nearly round holes that are taller than one layer into polyholes (polygons sized for the nozzle), which print closer to their true size.
hole_to_polyhole_threshold: How far points may be from a perfect circle and still count as a round hole. Models often store circles as uneven triangles, so some margin helps find them. In mm, or a percentage of the radius.
hole_to_polyhole_twisted: Rotate the polyhole a little every layer.
host_type: Kind of print host the printer uses, for uploading G-code to it.
hot_plate_temp: Bed temperature on the High Temp Plate after the first layer. 0 means this filament should not be printed on the High Temp Plate.
hot_plate_temp_initial_layer: Bed temperature on the High Temp Plate for the first layer. 0 means this filament should not be printed on the High Temp Plate.
idle_temperature: Nozzle temperature for a tool that is not in use on multi-tool printers, when ooze prevention is on. 0 turns it off.
independent_support_layer_height: Let support use its own layer height, separate from the part's, to tune the Z gap and save time. Not available with a prime tower.
infill_anchor: Length of the short wall pieces that connect infill lines to the walls. A percentage is taken from the infill line width. Nearby infill lines are joined along the wall where possible, and shorter connections than this are used where not. 0 leaves lines unconnected, 1000 means no limit.
infill_anchor_max: Longest wall piece used to connect infill lines to the walls. A percentage is taken from the infill line width. 0 connects only with simple short joins, 1000 means no limit.
infill_combination: Print sparse infill once every few layers, at a thicker layer height, to save time. Walls keep the normal layer height.
infill_combination_max_layer_height: Thickest layer the combined infill may use. 0 or 100% uses the nozzle diameter (fastest), around 80% gives stronger infill. The number of layers combined comes from this divided by the layer height.
infill_direction: Angle of the sparse infill lines (where the pattern starts or runs).
infill_lock_depth: How far the infill and the outer skin overlap, so they hold together.
infill_overhang_angle: Angle of the slanted infill lines. 60° gives a true honeycomb.
infill_shift_step: Shift each infill layer slightly, for a crossed texture.
infill_wall_overlap: Grows the infill a little into the walls so they bond. Percentage of the sparse infill line width. About 10 to 15% avoids too much plastic building up.
inherits: The parent profile this one is based on.
initial_layer_acceleration: Acceleration on the first layer. Lower values help it stick to the plate.
initial_layer_infill_speed: Speed of solid infill on the first layer.
initial_layer_line_width: Line width on the first layer. A percentage is taken from the nozzle diameter.
initial_layer_min_bead_width: Narrowest wall line on the first layer. About the nozzle size is best for adhesion.
initial_layer_print_height: Height of the first layer. A thicker first layer forgives an uneven plate and sticks better.
initial_layer_speed: Speed of the first layer, except its solid infill.
initial_layer_travel_acceleration: Travel acceleration on the first layer. A percentage is taken from the travel acceleration.
initial_layer_travel_jerk: Travel jerk on the first layer. A percentage is taken from the travel jerk.
initial_layer_travel_speed: Travel speed on the first layer.
inner_wall_filament_id: Which filament prints the inner walls. Default uses the filament of the object or part.
inner_wall_flow_ratio: Flow multiplier for inner walls, applied on top of the filament's flow ratio and the object's flow ratio.
inner_wall_line_width: Line width of inner walls. A percentage is taken from the nozzle diameter.
input_shaping_damp_x: Damping ratio of the X input shaper. 0 keeps the firmware's value. To turn input shaping off, set the type to Disable. On RepRapFirmware X and Y share one value.
input_shaping_damp_y: Damping ratio of the Y input shaper. 0 keeps the firmware's value. To turn input shaping off, set the type to Disable.
input_shaping_emit: Write the input shaping settings below into the G-code, replacing the firmware's. Off keeps the firmware's settings.
input_shaping_freq_x: Resonance frequency for the X input shaper. 0 keeps the firmware's value. To turn input shaping off, set the type to Disable. On RepRapFirmware X and Y share one value.
input_shaping_freq_y: Resonance frequency for the Y input shaper. 0 keeps the firmware's value. To turn input shaping off, set the type to Disable.
input_shaping_type: Input shaper algorithm. Default keeps the firmware's choice, Disable turns input shaping off.
interface_shells: Always print solid shells where two materials or volumes touch. Useful with clear materials on multi extruder printers, or with soluble support you add yourself.
interlocking_beam: Where two filaments touch, weave them together with small interlocking beams so the materials hold together, which helps most with materials that do not bond well.
interlocking_beam_layer_count: Height of each interlocking beam, in layers. Fewer layers is stronger but more likely to show flaws.
interlocking_boundary_avoidance: How far from the outside of the part (in beam cells) no interlocking is made, so it does not show.
interlocking_depth: How far into each material (in beam cells) the interlocking reaches from where they meet. Too little holds poorly.
internal_bridge_angle: Direction of internal bridge lines. 0 lets the slicer pick for each bridge. Any other angle is used as given (in plate coordinates, or turning with the model when "Align infill direction to model" is on).
internal_bridge_density: Spacing of internal bridge lines, the layer between sparse infill and the solid top layers, which matters a lot for the top surface. Above 100% (up to about 125%) gives a denser, flatter base. Below 100% saves material but can make the top worse.
internal_bridge_fan_speed: Part cooling fan speed for internal bridges. -1 uses the overhang fan settings. Less fan here than usual reduces warping from the extra cooling.
internal_bridge_flow: How much material internal bridges get. This is the first layer over the sparse infill, so a little more can make the part stronger and the top better. Above 1 adds material at the same spacing, below 1 uses less and thinner lines.
internal_bridge_speed: Speed of internal bridges. A percentage is taken from the bridge speed.
internal_solid_filament_id: Which filament prints internal solid infill. Default uses the filament of the object or part.
internal_solid_infill_acceleration: Acceleration of internal solid infill. A percentage is taken from the default acceleration.
internal_solid_infill_flow_ratio: Flow multiplier for internal solid infill, applied on top of the filament's flow ratio and the object's flow ratio.
internal_solid_infill_line_width: Line width of internal solid infill. A percentage is taken from the nozzle diameter.
internal_solid_infill_pattern: Line pattern of internal solid infill. Narrow areas use concentric instead when that detection is on.
internal_solid_infill_speed: Speed of internal solid infill (top and bottom surfaces have their own).
ironing_angle: Angle of the ironing lines, relative to the top surface lines.
ironing_angle_fixed: Use the ironing angle as a fixed direction on the plate instead of relative to the top surface.
ironing_expansion: Grow (positive) or shrink (negative) the ironed area.
ironing_fan_speed: Part cooling fan speed while ironing. Less than usual reduces clogging at the very low flow and gives a smoother finish. -1 keeps the normal fan speed.
ironing_flow: Amount of material while ironing, as a share of a normal layer's flow. Too much leaves an over extruded surface.
ironing_inset: How far ironing stays from the edges. 0 uses half the nozzle diameter.
ironing_type: Ironing goes over a flat surface a second time with very little flow to make it smooth. Choose where: no ironing, all top surfaces, only the topmost surface, or every solid layer.
is_infill_first: Print infill before walls. Walls first works best almost always. Infill first can help extreme overhangs, since the walls then have infill to lean on, but the infill may show through the outer surface.
lateral_lattice_angle_1: Tilt of the first set of lateral lattice members from vertical. 0 is vertical.
lateral_lattice_angle_2: Tilt of the second set of lateral lattice members from vertical. 0 is vertical.
layer_change_gcode: G-code added at every layer change, after the nozzle lifts to the next layer.
layer_height: Height of each layer. Thinner layers give finer detail and take longer.
lightning_overhang_angle: Steepest overhang that lightning infill branches may support.
lightning_prune_angle: How strongly short or unsupported lightning branches are cut back. Converted to a distance per layer.
lightning_straightening_angle: How much lightning branches may be straightened to keep them simple.
line_width: Line width used where a feature's own width is 0. A percentage is taken from the nozzle diameter.
long_retractions_when_cut: Pull the filament back further before cutting it at a filament change, which needs much less purging. Experimental: it raises the risk of clogs and other problems.
machine_end_gcode: G-code added when the whole print ends.
machine_load_filament_time: Time to load a new filament at a change, for the time estimate only. Mostly for single extruder multi material printers; usually 0 for tool changers.
machine_max_acceleration_travel: Highest acceleration while traveling (M204 T, Marlin 2 only).
machine_max_junction_deviation: Highest junction deviation (M205 J). Used by Marlin when above 0. Set 0 if your Marlin 2 printer uses classic jerk.
machine_pause_gcode: G-code that pauses the print. You can insert it at a layer from the preview.
machine_start_gcode: G-code added at the start of the whole print.
machine_tool_change_time: Time to change tools, for the time estimate only. Mostly for tool changers; usually 0 for single extruder multi material printers.
machine_unload_filament_time: Time to unload the old filament at a change, for the time estimate only. Mostly for single extruder multi material printers; usually 0 for tool changers.
make_overhang_printable: Change the shape of steep overhangs so they print without support.
make_overhang_printable_angle: Steepest overhang left after the change. 90° changes nothing, 0 turns every overhang into a cone.
make_overhang_printable_hole_size: Holes in the base bigger than this area are left open; smaller ones are filled with a cone. 0 fills every hole.
manual_filament_change: For changing filament by hand: the change filament G-code is used only once at the start, and tool change commands (like T0) are left out of the whole print. Use it with pauses you add for each swap.
master_extruder_id: Extruder that filaments go to by default.
max_bridge_length: Bridges up to this long print without support. 0 supports every bridge, a very large value supports none.
max_layer_height: Thickest layer this extruder can print. Limits adaptive layer height.
max_resonance_avoidance_speed: Top of the speed range skipped to avoid the printer's resonance.
max_travel_detour_distance: When avoiding crossing walls, don't take a detour longer than this. In mm, or a percentage of the direct path. 0 means no limit.
max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope: Smooths sudden changes in flow, for example from fast wide lines to slow thin ones. The nozzle cannot change its pressure instantly, so a sudden change gives a blob or a thin spot. The value is the largest flow change allowed per second (mm³/s²). 0 turns it off.
max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_segm: Length of the pieces the smoothing splits lines into. Shorter gives smoother changes but a much bigger G-code file. 3 mm suits most printers.
min_bead_width: Width of the wall that replaces thin features (see minimum feature size). If the feature is thinner than this, the wall is widened to this. Percentage of the nozzle diameter.
min_feature_size: Thinnest feature that is still printed. Thinner ones are left out, and anything thicker gets at least the minimum wall width. Percentage of the nozzle diameter.
min_layer_height: Thinnest layer this extruder can print. Limits adaptive layer height.
min_length_factor: Leave out short open wall pieces shorter than this, which mostly waste time. Higher values remove more. Top and bottom surfaces keep theirs, so nothing visible goes missing.
min_resonance_avoidance_speed: Bottom of the speed range skipped to avoid the printer's resonance.
min_skirt_length: Print at least this much filament in the skirt, adding loops if needed. 0 turns it off. Useful when the start G-code has no purge line.
min_width_top_surface: Top surfaces narrower than this (where another layer partly covers them) are not treated as top surfaces, so "Only one wall on top surfaces" does not apply to them. In mm, or a percentage of the line width.
minimum_sparse_infill_area: Sparse infill areas smaller than this become solid infill.
mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth: How deep the painted color regions interlock with each other. Ignored when the max width is 0 or smaller than this. 0 turns it off.
mmu_segmented_region_max_width: Deepest a painted color region reaches into the part. 0 turns the limit off.
notes: Your own notes. They are also written into the G-code header.
nozzle_hrc: Hardness of the nozzle. Abrasive filaments need a hard nozzle. 0 skips the hardness check.
nozzle_temperature: Nozzle temperature after the first layer.
nozzle_temperature_initial_layer: Nozzle temperature for the first layer with this filament.
nozzle_type: Material of the nozzle. It decides how well it resists abrasive filaments and which filaments it can print.
nozzle_volume: Volume inside the nozzle between the cutter and the tip.
nozzle_volume_type: Type of each extruder's nozzle: standard or high flow.
only_one_wall_first_layer: Print only one wall on the first layer, leaving more room for the bottom pattern.
only_one_wall_top: Print only one wall on flat top surfaces, leaving more room for the top pattern.
ooze_prevention: Lower the temperature of extruders that are not in use, so they don't ooze.
outer_wall_acceleration: Acceleration of the outer wall. Lower values give a cleaner surface.
outer_wall_filament_id: Which filament prints the outer walls. Default uses the filament of the object or part.
outer_wall_flow_ratio: Flow multiplier for outer walls, applied on top of the filament's flow ratio and the object's flow ratio.
outer_wall_line_width: Line width of the outer wall. A percentage is taken from the nozzle diameter.
outer_wall_speed: Speed of the outer, visible wall. Usually slower than the inner walls for a better surface.
overhang_1_4_speed: Speed of wall lines that overhang 10 to 25% of their width. 0 keeps the normal wall speed.
overhang_2_4_speed: Speed of wall lines that overhang 25 to 50% of their width. 0 keeps the normal wall speed.
overhang_3_4_speed: Speed of wall lines that overhang 50 to 75% of their width. 0 keeps the normal wall speed.
overhang_4_4_speed: Speed of wall lines that overhang 75 to 100% of their width. 0 keeps the normal wall speed.
overhang_fan_speed: Part cooling fan speed for bridges and for walls that overhang more than the threshold above. More cooling there makes them sag and curl less.
overhang_fan_threshold: Walls that overhang more than this (the share of the line width with nothing below it) use the overhang fan speed. 0% applies it to every outer wall, whether it overhangs or not.
overhang_flow_ratio: Flow multiplier for overhangs, applied on top of the filament's flow ratio and the object's flow ratio.
overhang_reverse: On even layers, print walls that hang over something in the opposite direction. Alternating the direction can greatly improve steep overhangs, and it also spreads the stresses that cause warping.
overhang_reverse_internal_only: Reverse only the inner walls, not the outer one. Still spreads the stresses (less warping) while the outer surface stays even.
overhang_reverse_threshold: How far a wall must overhang before it is reversed, in mm or a percentage of the wall width. 0 reverses every even layer. Without overhang wall detection this is ignored and every even layer is reversed.
parallel_printheads_bed_exclude_areas: Bed areas to keep empty for each number of parallel printheads: the first item for one head, the second for two, and so on. Leave an item empty for none.
parallel_printheads_count: Number of printheads that print side by side at the same time, on printers built for it.
parking_pos_retraction: Distance from the nozzle tip to where the filament is parked when unloaded. Must match the printer's firmware.
part_cooling_fan_min_pwm: Some fans won't start below a certain power. Any fan speed above 0 is raised to at least this, so the fan always starts. 0 still turns the fan off.
pellet_flow_coefficient: Flow factor for pellet printers, found by testing. It is turned into an equivalent filament diameter (filament_diameter = sqrt(4 × coefficient / π)), and all other flow calculations stay the same.
pellet_modded_printer: The printer prints from pellets instead of filament.
physical_extruder_map: Which physical extruder each extruder in the profile refers to.
post_process: Scripts that run over the G-code after slicing. Give their full paths, separated by semicolons. Each script gets the G-code file's path as its first argument and can change the file in place.
precise_outer_wall: Adjusts the spacing of the outer wall so the part's outside is more accurate, which also makes layers more even. Ignored with the outer-inner or inner-outer-inner wall orders.
precise_z_height: Fine tunes the last few layers so the part comes out at its exact height. Experimental.
preferred_orientation: Rotate STL files around Z by this much when they are first imported.
preheat_steps: Number of preheat commands (such as M104.1) to add. Only for the Prusa XL; use 1 for other printers.
preheat_time: Start heating the next tool this many seconds before it is needed, while the current tool is still printing, so tool changes wait less. Adds an M104 for the next tool.
preset_names: Profiles that belong to this physical printer.
pressure_advance: Pressure advance (Klipper), also called linear advance (Marlin). It makes up for the delay between pushing filament and plastic coming out, for sharper corners and even lines.
prime_tower_brim_width: Brim width of the prime tower. A negative value picks the width from the tower's height.
prime_tower_enable_framework: Add ribs inside the prime tower so it stands more firmly.
prime_tower_infill_gap: Gap between the prime tower's infill lines.
prime_tower_skip_points: Leave out the prime tower wall where the wipe path starts.
prime_volume: Amount of filament used to prime the extruder on the tower.
print_extruder_id: Extruder this process is set up for.
print_extruder_variant: Extruder variant this process is set up for.
print_flow_ratio: Scales all extrusion of this process. Plastics change volume as they melt and cool, so the right amount varies a little. Usually between 0.95 and 1.05.
print_host: Address of the print host (host name, IP or URL) that G-code is uploaded to. A host behind HAProxy with basic sign-in can be reached as user:password@address.
print_host_webui: Address of the printer's own web page, if it differs from the print host.
print_order: Order of the objects within a layer: the default order, or the order of the object list.
print_sequence: Print layer by layer across all objects, or one whole object after another.
printable_height: Tallest the printer can print, set by its mechanics.
printer_agent: Which network connection is used to talk to the printer.
printer_notes: Your own notes about the printer.
printer_structure: How the printer is built (CoreXY, bed slinger, H-bot, delta).
printer_technology: Kind of printer: filament (FFF) or resin (SLA).
printer_variant: Name of this variant of the printer, for example by nozzle size.
printhost_apikey: API key or password the print host needs for uploads.
printhost_cafile: A custom CA certificate (crt or pem) for HTTPS connections to OctoPrint. Empty uses the system's certificates.
printhost_port: Name of the printer on the print host.
printhost_ssl_ignore_revoke: Skip the HTTPS certificate revocation check, for example with self signed certificates when the connection otherwise fails.
printing_by_object_gcode: G-code added between objects when printing one object at a time.
process_change_extrusion_role_gcode: G-code from the process added whenever the kind of line being printed changes. Runs after the printer's and the filament's.
purge_in_prime_tower: Purge leftover filament into the prime tower.
raft_contact_distance: Gap between the raft and the part. Ignored when the support top Z distance is 0; the part then sits right on the raft.
raft_expansion: Grow every raft layer by this much in X and Y.
raft_first_layer_density: Density of the first raft or support layer.
raft_first_layer_expansion: Grow the first raft or support layer by this much, for better adhesion.
raft_layers: Raise the part on this many support layers. Helps materials like ABS that warp.
reduce_crossing_wall: Travel around walls instead of over them, which avoids marks on the surface.
reduce_fan_stop_start_freq: Never stop the part cooling fan completely; keep it at least at the minimum speed, so it switches on and off less often.
reduce_infill_retraction: Skip retraction for travel that stays inside infill, where oozing can't be seen. Fewer retractions save time on complex parts, but slicing takes longer.
relative_bridge_angle: Add the bridge angle to the automatically found bridge direction instead of replacing it.
resolution: Outlines are simplified to this precision before paths are made, to avoid needless points and G-code lines. Smaller is more precise and slices slower.
resonance_avoidance: Keep the outer wall speed out of the printer's resonance range, which avoids ringing on the surface. Turn off when testing for ringing.
retract_before_wipe: Part of the retraction done quickly before wiping, as a percentage of the retraction length.
retract_length_toolchange: How far filament is pulled back before a tool change (measured on the filament before the extruder).
retract_lift_above: Lift Z only above this height. 0 lifts everywhere.
retract_lift_below: Lift Z only below this height. 0 lifts everywhere.
retract_lift_enforce: On which surfaces Z lift is used: all, only top, only bottom, or top and bottom. The height limits above still apply.
retract_restart_extra: Push this much extra filament after a retraction, before printing again. Rarely needed.
retract_restart_extra_toolchange: Push this much extra filament after a tool change, before printing again.
retract_when_changing_layer: Always retract when moving to the next layer.
retraction_distances_when_cut: How far to pull the filament back before cutting it at a filament change. Experimental.
retraction_length: How far filament is pulled back before travel moves, so it doesn't ooze. 0 turns retraction off.
retraction_minimum_travel: Retract only for travel moves longer than this.
retraction_speed: Speed of pulling filament back from the nozzle.
role_based_wipe_speed: Wipe at the speed of the line just printed (for example, right after an outer wall, at the outer wall speed).
scan_first_layer: Use the printer's camera to check the first layer.
scarf_angle_threshold: With conditional scarf joints, use a scarf seam on walls whose sharpest corner is gentler than this angle (no sharp corner to hide the seam in).
scarf_joint_speed: Speed of scarf joints. Slow (under 100 mm/s) works best; if it differs a lot from the wall speed, turn on extrusion rate smoothing. A percentage is taken from the wall speed.
scarf_overhang_threshold: With conditional scarf joints, use them only on walls that overhang less than this share.
seam_gap: Stops each closed loop slightly short of where it started, which makes the seam less visible. In mm, or a percentage of the nozzle diameter.
seam_position: Where each outer wall loop starts: nearest to the last position, lined up, lined up at the back, at the back, or random.
seam_slope_conditional: Use scarf joints only on smooth walls, where there is no sharp corner to hide a normal seam in.
seam_slope_entire_loop: Spread the scarf along the whole wall loop.
seam_slope_inner_walls: Use scarf joints on inner walls too.
seam_slope_min_length: Length of the scarf. 0 turns it off.
seam_slope_start_height: Height where the scarf starts, in mm or a percentage of the layer height.
seam_slope_steps: Fewest pieces each scarf is printed in.
seam_slope_type: A scarf joint ramps the start and end of each loop over each other instead of butting them together, which hides the seam and makes it stronger. Choose where: on outer walls, on outer walls and holes, or nowhere. Beta.
set_other_flow_ratios: Set separate flow ratios for the other kinds of lines.
silent_mode: The printer has a silent mode, which prints with lower accelerations.
single_extruder_multi_material: The printer prints several filaments through one nozzle.
single_extruder_multi_material_priming: At the start of the print, prime every extruder that will be used along the front edge of the bed.
single_loop_draft_shield: After the first layer, print the skirt or draft shield with only one loop. Saves filament but may crack or warp.
skeleton_infill_density: Density of the skeleton, the inner part that is left after taking away the skin. Parts with the same infill settings but a different skeleton density are printed as separate regions.
skin_infill_density: Density of the skin, the outer layer of infill just inside the walls. Parts with the same infill settings but a different skin density are printed as separate regions.
skirt_distance: Gap between the skirt and the brim or the part.
skirt_height: Number of layers of skirt. Usually one.
skirt_loops: Number of skirt loops. 0 means no skirt.
skirt_speed: Speed of the skirt. 0 uses the layer's normal speed.
skirt_start_angle: Where the skirt starts, as an angle around the part's center. 0 is straight to the right, counterclockwise is positive.
skirt_type: One skirt around all parts together, or one per part.
slice_closing_radius: Closes cracks in the model up to twice this size while slicing. Larger values can blur fine detail, so keep it small.
slicing_mode: How the model is cut into layers. Even-odd suits the 3DLabPrint airplane models. Close holes closes every hole in the model.
slow_down_for_layer_cooling: Print short layers slower so each takes at least the layer time set here, giving it time to cool.
slow_down_layer_time: Layers that would print faster than this are slowed down, so they cool better.
slow_down_layers: Print the first few layers slower, speeding up evenly over this many layers.
slow_down_min_speed: Slowest the print may get when slowing down for layer cooling.
slowdown_for_curled_perimeters: Print slower where walls may have curled up, such as overhangs at sharp corners (like the bow of a Benchy), so they curl less over the layers.
small_area_infill_flow_compensation: Adjust the flow on small infill areas, where short lines tend to over extrude. Beta.
small_area_infill_flow_compensation_mode: The flow adjustment for small areas, one pair per line: line length, flow factor (for example 0,0 and 0.2,0.4 up to 10,1). Lengths between the pairs are blended.
small_perimeter_speed: Speed of small loops (radius up to the small perimeter threshold), usually holes. A percentage is taken from the outer wall speed. 0 picks one automatically.
small_perimeter_threshold: Loops up to this radius count as small perimeters.
solid_infill_direction: Angle of the solid infill lines.
solid_infill_rotate_template: Rotate the solid infill a set amount on each layer, from a list of angles such as 0,90. The first angle is used on the first layer, the next on the second, and the list repeats. Overrides the usual alternating direction.
spaghetti_detector: Use the printer's camera to watch for spaghetti (a failed print).
sparse_infill_acceleration: Acceleration of sparse infill. A percentage is taken from the default acceleration.
sparse_infill_density: How full the inside of the part is. 100% makes it solid, using the internal solid infill pattern.
sparse_infill_filament_id: Which filament prints sparse infill. Default uses the filament of the object or part.
sparse_infill_flow_ratio: Flow multiplier for sparse infill, applied on top of the filament's flow ratio and the object's flow ratio.
sparse_infill_line_width: Line width of sparse infill. A percentage is taken from the nozzle diameter.
sparse_infill_pattern: Pattern of the infill inside the part.
sparse_infill_rotate_template: Rotate the sparse infill on each layer from a list of angles, such as 0,30,60,90. The list repeats when it runs out. +5 turns 5° more than the previous layer.
spiral_finishing_flow_ratio: Flow at the very end of the spiral. The last loop normally fades the flow from 100% to 0%, which can leave the end thin; a value here sets where the fade ends.
spiral_mode: Vase mode: prints the part as one continuous spiral wall over solid bottom layers, with no seam. Turns a solid model into a single wall.
spiral_mode_max_xy_smoothing: How far points may move in X and Y to smooth the spiral. A percentage is taken from the nozzle diameter.
spiral_mode_smooth: Also smooth X and Y, so even slanted walls show no seam.
spiral_starting_flow_ratio: Flow at the very start of the spiral. The first loop normally fades the flow in from 0% to 100%, which can leave the start thin; a value here sets where the fade starts.
staggered_inner_seams: Shift each inner wall's seam back a little more than the one outside it, in a zigzag, so the seams don't stack.
standby_temperature_delta: How much an extruder cools while it is not in use. Not used when the filament sets an idle temperature.
start_end_points: Start and end of the path from the cutter to the waste chute.
supertack_plate_temp: Bed temperature on the Cool Plate SuperTack after the first layer. 0 means this filament should not be printed on it.
supertack_plate_temp_initial_layer: Bed temperature on the Cool Plate SuperTack for the first layer. 0 means this filament should not be printed on it.
support_air_filtration: The printer has air filtration (controlled with M106 P3 S0-255).
support_angle: Rotate the support pattern by this angle.
support_base_pattern: Pattern of the support. Default is hollow (no base pattern) for tree supports and rectilinear for the others. Organic supports print their two walls with the base pattern only when it is not hollow.
support_bottom_interface_spacing: Distance between bottom interface lines. 0 makes the interface solid.
support_bottom_z_distance: Gap between the part and support standing on it. Ignored when the top Z distance is 0 and the bottom has interface layers; the support then touches the part.
support_chamber_temp_control: The printer can control its chamber temperature (with M141 S).
support_critical_regions_only: Support only the critical areas, such as sharp tails and cantilevers.
support_expansion: Grow (+) or shrink (-) normal support sideways.
support_filament: Which filament prints the support base and raft. Default uses the part's filament.
support_flow_ratio: Flow multiplier for support, applied on top of the filament's flow ratio and the object's flow ratio.
support_interface_bottom_layers: Number of interface layers at the bottom of the support, where it stands on the part.
support_interface_filament: Which filament prints the support interface. Default uses the part's filament.
support_interface_flow_ratio: Flow multiplier for the support interface, applied on top of the filament's flow ratio and the object's flow ratio.
support_interface_loop_pattern: Cover the top contact layer of the support with loops.
support_interface_not_for_body: Where possible, don't use the interface filament for the support base (it is often an expensive or soluble one).
support_interface_pattern: Pattern of the support interface. Default is rectilinear for normal interfaces and concentric for soluble ones.
support_interface_spacing: Distance between top interface lines. 0 makes the interface solid, which is also used when support ironing is on.
support_interface_top_layers: Number of interface layers at the top of the support, under the part.
support_ironing: Iron the support interface (go over it again with very little flow) so the surface printed on it comes out smoother. The interface is then printed solid.
support_ironing_flow: Amount of material while ironing the support interface, as a share of its normal flow. Too much over extrudes.
support_line_width: Line width of support. A percentage is taken from the nozzle diameter.
support_material_interface_fan_speed: Part cooling fan speed for support interfaces. More fan than usual weakens the bond between support and part, so the support comes off more easily. -1 keeps the normal fan speed.
support_multi_bed_types: The printer can use several kinds of build plate.
support_object_first_layer_gap: Sideways gap between the part and its support on the first layer.
support_object_xy_distance: Sideways gap between the part and its support.
support_on_build_plate_only: Only build support up from the plate, never on the part itself.
support_parallel_printheads: Show the settings for printers that print with several heads side by side.
support_remove_small_overhang: Skip support for small overhangs that will probably print fine without it.
support_style: Shape of the support. Normal support as a grid is sturdier; snug follows the part closely, uses less material and leaves fewer marks. For tree support, slim branches merge more and save material, strong branches stay apart for stability, hybrid mixes normal support under large flat overhangs, and organic grows smooth branches.
support_threshold_angle: Overhangs flatter than this angle (measured from horizontal) get support. A smaller value means steeper overhangs print without support. With 0, normal support uses the threshold overlap instead.
support_threshold_overlap: When the threshold angle is 0: overhangs whose overlap with the layer below is less than this get support. In mm, or a percentage of the line width.
support_top_z_distance: Gap between the top of the support and the part. 0 for soluble support, about 0.1 mm for semi detachable, 0.2 mm for easy removal.
support_type: Normal or tree support, made automatically (auto) or only where you placed support enforcers (manual).
symmetric_infill_y_axis: For two parts that mirror each other across the Y axis: turn this on for one of them to mirror its infill texture too.
temperature_vitrification: Temperature at which the filament softens. When the bed is this hot or hotter, open the front door or lift the lid to avoid clogs.
textured_cool_plate_temp: Bed temperature on the Textured Cool Plate after the first layer. 0 means this filament should not be printed on it.
textured_cool_plate_temp_initial_layer: Bed temperature on the Textured Cool Plate for the first layer. 0 means this filament should not be printed on it.
textured_plate_temp: Bed temperature on the Textured PEI Plate after the first layer. 0 means this filament should not be printed on it.
textured_plate_temp_initial_layer: Bed temperature on the Textured PEI Plate for the first layer. 0 means this filament should not be printed on it.
thick_bridges: Print visible bridges as tall as the nozzle is wide. Stronger and more reliable over longer spans, but they look rougher. Off gives better looking bridges that only manage shorter spans.
thick_internal_bridges: Print internal bridges as tall as the nozzle is wide. Stronger and more reliable over sparse infill, but the top surface can look worse. Off can look better but is less reliable.
thumbnails: Preview picture sizes stored in the G-code file, written "XxY, XxY, ...".
thumbnails_format: Format of the preview pictures: PNG looks best, JPG is smallest, QOI suits firmware with little memory, and the others are for specific screens.
time_cost: Cost of running the printer per hour, for the cost estimate.
timelapse_type: Make a timelapse video of each print from the printer's camera, one picture per layer. Smooth moves the head out of the way for each picture (needs a prime tower to keep the parts clean); traditional takes the picture wherever the head is.
tool_change_on_wipe_tower: Move to the wipe tower before each tool change command (Tx). Only for printers with several toolheads using the type 2 tower, which otherwise skip this travel.
top_bottom_infill_wall_overlap: Grows the top solid infill slightly into the walls so they bond and no pinholes show along the edges. 25 to 30% is a good start. Percentage of the top surface line width.
top_shell_layers: Number of solid layers at the top, counting the top surface. If these layers end up thinner than the top shell thickness, more are added.
top_shell_thickness: Smallest total thickness of the top solid layers. When the layer count gives less than this (for example with very thin layers), more layers are added. 0 turns this off, so only the layer count decides.
top_solid_infill_flow_ratio: Flow multiplier for the top surface. A little less can give a smoother top. Applied on top of the filament's flow ratio and the object's flow ratio.
top_surface_acceleration: Acceleration of the top surface. Lower values can give a nicer top.
top_surface_density: How densely the top surface is filled. 100% gives a solid, smooth top. Less gives a textured top in the chosen pattern, and 0% prints only the walls on the top layer.
top_surface_filament_id: Which filament prints the top surface. Default uses the filament of the object or part.
top_surface_line_width: Line width of top surfaces. A percentage is taken from the nozzle diameter.
top_surface_pattern: Line pattern of the top surface.
top_surface_speed: Speed of the solid top surface.
travel_slope: Angle of the climb for slope and spiral Z hops. 90° lifts straight up.
travel_speed: Speed of travel moves (moving without printing).
travel_speed_z: Speed of moves up and down. Usually lower, since the bed or gantry is heavy to move. 0 uses the travel speed, limited by what the printer can do.
tree_support_angle_slow: Angle the branches prefer when they don't need to steer around the part. Lower is more upright and stable, higher merges branches sooner.
tree_support_auto_brim: Work out the tree support's brim width automatically.
tree_support_branch_angle: Steepest overhang angle the tree branches may lean at. A larger angle lets branches lean more and reach further.
tree_support_branch_angle_organic: Steepest overhang angle the organic branches may lean at. A larger angle lets branches lean more and reach further.
tree_support_branch_diameter: Diameter of the branches where they start.
tree_support_branch_diameter_angle: How quickly branches get thicker toward the bottom. 0 keeps them the same thickness all the way; a little angle makes organic support more stable.
tree_support_branch_diameter_organic: Diameter of the organic branches where they start.
tree_support_branch_distance_organic: Distance between neighboring organic branch points.
tree_support_brim_width: Distance from a tree trunk to the outermost line of its brim.
tree_support_tip_diameter: Diameter of the branch tips (organic support).
tree_support_top_rate: How dense the support is right under the part where branches end. Higher supports overhangs better but is harder to remove, so top interface layers are usually the better choice.
tree_support_wall_count: Number of walls on tree support, 0 to 2. 0 picks automatically.
tree_support_with_infill: Add infill inside the large hollow parts of tree support.
use_3mf: Send the print to the printer as a .gcode.3mf file instead of plain G-code, for printers that take 3MF jobs.
use_firmware_retraction: Let the firmware do retractions with G10 and G11 commands. Only recent Marlin supports it. Experimental.
use_relative_e_distances: Write extrusion as relative amounts. Recommended for most printers, needed for the wipe tower, and best with object labels. A few printers work better with absolute amounts.
wall_direction: Direction the outer wall loops run, seen from above. Holes run the other way so they stay in line with layers where the outline changes.
wall_distribution_count: Over how many walls (counting from the middle) width changes are spread. Lower values keep the outer walls at their normal width.
wall_generator: Classic makes walls of fixed width and fills thin spots with gap fill. Arachne varies the wall width to fit the shape.
wall_loops: Number of walls on every layer.
wall_maximum_deviation: How far a simplified wall may stray from the true outline when short segments are merged. Larger gives smaller G-code but less accuracy, and it limits the maximum wall resolution.
wall_maximum_resolution: Shortest wall segment kept. Smaller values give more precise walls.
wall_sequence: Order of the walls. Inner then outer gives the best overhangs, because the outer wall leans on the inner one, but the outer surface is slightly less accurate. Outer then inner gives the most accurate outside. Inner, outer, inner gives both a clean outside and good overhangs, and needs at least three walls.
wall_transition_angle: When to switch between an even and odd number of walls in narrowing wedges. Wedges wider than this angle get no switch and no wall in the middle. Lower values mean fewer and shorter switches, which can leave small gaps.
wall_transition_filter_deviation: Keeps the wall count from flipping back and forth between one more and one less wall. A larger margin flips less often but allows more variation in width.
wall_transition_length: Space used to split or join walls where the wall count changes as the part gets thinner. Percentage of the nozzle diameter.
wipe: Move the nozzle back along the last line while retracting, to wipe off any plastic that leaked. Reduces blobs after travel.
wipe_before_external_loop: With the outer then inner or inner, outer, inner wall orders, start the outer wall a little inside the part so any blob from pushing the filament back is hidden.
wipe_distance: How far the nozzle moves along the last line while wiping. Any retraction left over when the wipe ends is done in place.
wipe_on_loops: Move the nozzle a little inward before leaving a closed loop, which hides the seam.
wipe_speed: Speed of wiping. A percentage is taken from the travel speed.
wipe_tower_bridging: Longest gap between supports in the tower's sparse layers.
wipe_tower_cone_angle: Angle at the tip of the cone that steadies the tower. A larger angle gives a wider base.
wipe_tower_extra_flow: Extra flow for the purge lines on the tower, making them thicker or thinner. Their spacing adjusts to match.
wipe_tower_extra_rib_length: Make the tower's rib walls longer (positive) or shorter (negative). They never get smaller than the purge volume needs.
wipe_tower_extra_spacing: Spacing of the purge lines on the tower.
wipe_tower_filament: Which extruder prints the tower's outer wall. 0 uses whichever is loaded, preferring a non soluble one.
wipe_tower_fillet_wall: Round the corners of the tower's wall.
wipe_tower_max_purge_speed: Fastest speed for purging on the tower and for its sparse layers. The lower of this, the sparse infill speed and the speed allowed by the filament's max flow is used.
wipe_tower_no_sparse_layers: Skip the tower on layers with no tool change; on layers with a change the nozzle goes down to print it. Make sure the head can't hit the print. Beta.
wipe_tower_rib_width: Width of the tower's ribs, always less than half the tower's side.
wipe_tower_rotation_angle: Rotation of the tower relative to the X axis.
wipe_tower_type: Which wipe tower is used. Type 1 suits Bambu and Qidi printers with a filament cutter. Type 2 works better with tool changers and MMU printers and is steadier overall.
wipe_tower_wall_type: Shape of the tower's outer wall: a plain rectangle, a cone with a rounded foot for stability, or a wall with four ribs for strength.
wipe_tower_x: X position of the tower's front left corner.
wipe_tower_y: Y position of the tower's front left corner.
wiping_volumes_extruders: Purge amounts when loading or unloading each extruder, used to fill in the full purge table more easily.
wrapping_detection_layers: Layers on which the printer checks for filament clumping.
wrapping_exclude_area: Area left out of the clumping check.
xy_contour_compensation: Make the outside of the part bigger (positive) or smaller (negative) by this much, to fine tune sizes for parts that fit together.
xy_hole_compensation: Make holes bigger (positive) or smaller (negative) by this much, to fine tune sizes for parts that fit together.
z_hop: How far the nozzle lifts after retracting, so it clears the print during travel. Spiral lifts can also reduce stringing.
z_hop_types: How the nozzle lifts: automatic, straight up, on a slope, or in a spiral.
z_offset: Added to every Z position in the G-code, to make up for a Z endstop that is slightly off. For example, if zero leaves the nozzle 0.3 mm above the plate, use -0.3.
zaa_dont_alternate_fill_direction: Don't alternate the fill direction between layers when Z contouring is on.
zaa_enabled: Z contouring (Z anti-aliasing): tilts the top surfaces' lines up and down within the layer to follow the model's slope, which hides the stair steps on gently curved tops.
zaa_min_z: Smallest height step Z contouring uses. Also sets where the layers are cut.
zaa_minimize_perimeter_height: Lower the top walls to the height of the model's edge on slopes flatter than this angle. About 35 works well, 0 turns it off.
